title: Resume ALSA playback after a USB DAC replug
problem: During a USB DAC outage, the ALSA sink consumes and discards audio to keep the sync task moving, but the discarded frames remain in its buffered-frame accounting. The first real timestamp after reopening projects playback ahead by the entire outage and starts a repeated hard-sync/XRUN cycle.
reproduce: Model the reporter's 14-second outage at 48 kHz. The pinned baseline has no way to retire the resulting 672,000 accepted-but-discarded frames when the PCM returns.
acceptance: The discarded gap is counted without overflow, returned exactly once on recovery, and the ALSA sink reports it before the first real post-recovery write. The focused baseline fails and the unchanged test passes on the candidate.
repair: Accumulate frames discarded during device loss in SinkRecovery and publish one playback-progress update outside the device mutex immediately after ALSA successfully reopens.

verification.limitations: BCL proves the outage-frame accounting with the reporter's exact 14-second/48-kHz scale and checks overflow behavior. A separate Debian build compiled the ALSA backend and passed all 18 recovery tests. Only the reporter can confirm continuous sound on the physical OpenWrt USB DAC.
verification.ownerCheck: Build PR #55 for the reported OpenWrt target, play from Music Assistant, unplug the USB DAC for about five seconds, reconnect it, and confirm continuous playback resumes without periodic XRUNs or Lost sync/Regained sync cycling.

selection.reason: Revalidate our already published draft PR against the pinned baseline and capture reproducible evidence without authorizing a competing publication.

publish.commitMessage: Fix ALSA playback clock after device recovery
